To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we developed a new approach to transcribe printed books using the human effort that was previously wasted in solving CAPTCHAs.

(i) humans can perform the task of digitizing printed material at a high level of accuracy and speed; (ii) this task is a natural extension to the security measures that users already perform when they visit Web sites; and (iii) this task can be done at no cost to users and without requiring them to install any additional software.

we developed a method for digitizing old printed material by using human effort to recognize characters in scanned images that computerized optical recognition failed to recognize, and that this method can match the quality of professional human transcription.

the following questions: (a) Can human effort be channeled towards useful purposes? (b) Can the Web be used as a platform for harnessing such effort? (c) What are the challenges of such an approach? (d) How can we overcome these challenges? (e) How can we scale up this approach to handle large amounts of data?

reCAPTCHA is a human based character recognition system which is used to prevent spamming in web applications and also used to help in digitizing old books.
reCAPTCHA, the CAPTCHA service we created, is a successful example of a system that uses human effort to solve a difficult computational problem.
we have shown that human based character recognition can be done on the web, at large scale, with very high accuracy, at a low cost, and in real time.
